transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I’m mostly here because my family and everyone else keeps saying I’ve been doing too much. 

But to me, it just feels like I’m the only one around with enough drive to actually get things done. We have a move to handle, and I'm the one rebuilding the new garage so it gets done right. I've also been organizing some things over at the church, and... well, I still have to show the younger fellows at the plant how the grinding and mixing jobs actually ought to be done. I'm just getting it all handled, but they wanted me to come talk to you.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt significantly low, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I can't say that I have. I don't really get down in the dumps or feel hopeless like that. There's just... well, there's always too much work to be done to sit around losing interest in things. I just keep moving and get on with it.
Have you ever felt so energetic or active that you ended up in trouble at work, or had people tell you that you were acting out of touch with reality?

Well, I suppose... yes, there's been some trouble lately. At work, they actually pulled me off the floor after a safety incident. I was just trying to get things moving faster, but they didn't see it that way. And at home... well, my wife and the kids, they've stopped trusting me with things. They took over the decisions about the money, and driving, and even the details for the move. They say things got out of hand, but I was just trying to get it all sorted out.
When you say your family felt things got out of hand, did they ever mention that you were seeing or hearing things that weren't there, or perhaps believing things that others told you weren't true?

No, no, nothing like that. Nobody's ever said I was seeing things or hearing voices, and I don't believe crazy things. I mean, they think I'm doing too much, sure, but they don't think I'm... you know, losing my mind or imagining things. I just have big plans and I want to see them through.

Looking back over your entire life, even many years ago, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt deeply depressed, hopeless, or lost all interest in your usual activities?

No, like I said a minute ago... I really haven't. Even looking way back. I've worked the grinders and mixers most of my life, and... well, I just never had a time where I felt hopeless or stopped caring about things for weeks on end. I've always just kept moving and stayed busy.
During these times when you feel you have all this extra drive and energy, how many hours of sleep are you typically getting at night?

Well, I haven't really been paying close attention to the exact hours. I mean, when I've got a lot going on and I'm focused on getting things done, I just sleep when I need to and get back to it. I couldn't tell you a specific number.
During these periods of high energy, have you ever had to be hospitalized because of your behavior?
No, I've never been in the hospital for anything like that. Never had to go to the hospital because of how I was acting, no. I just stay busy, like I said.
When you have these periods of high energy and drive, how many days in a row would you say this usually lasts?
Well, this current stretch... it's been going on for about a month now. Ever since we were forced to start packing up and leaving the old house. I've just been going non-stop since then.
During these times when you feel you have all this extra drive, do you find that you feel much more important, talented, or powerful than you usually do?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm anyone special or anything like that. I'm just a guy trying to get things done, you know? I don't feel like I have superpowers or anything, I just have a lot of energy to keep moving.
During these times when you have all this energy, do you find that you talk so much faster than usual that people have a hard time keeping up with you?

Yeah, I do. Once I start explaining what needs doing with all this packing, the words just keep coming out. My family says I talk over them so fast that they can’t even get a word in to tell me to stop.

Looking back over the years, would you say that this 'go-go-go' pace is just how you are almost all the time, or is it something that comes and goes, where you have periods of high energy followed by times when you are much more like your usual self?

Well, I'm not really sure. I mean, I don't think I'm like this all the time, but... I haven't really kept track of it over the years. I couldn't tell you for sure if it comes and goes in phases or anything like that. I just know how I've been feeling lately with all this packing.
Can you think of any times in your life where you felt significantly less energetic and driven than you do right now, even if you weren't feeling 'down'?

I don't really know. I mean, I guess there must have been times when I was slower, but I can't really point to a specific time. Right now, I just know I have this energy and I need to use it. I don't really sit around thinking about when I had less energy.

When you look at your life as a whole, are there significant periods of time where you felt like you were just at your normal, baseline self—not having all this extra 'go-go-go' energy, but also not feeling slow or down?

I honestly couldn't tell you. I mean, I'm 74 years old, I've worked hard my whole life... I don't really sit and analyze my moods like that. I'm sure I've had normal days, or normal years, but I just don't pay attention to it. I'm just focused on getting everything packed up right now.
Looking back over the years, have your family or friends ever told you that you were acting like a completely different person compared to how you usually are?

I don't really... no, nobody has ever said that to me. I mean, my wife knows how I get when I have a big project to do, but she's never told me I was acting like a completely different person. People mostly just let me work. So, no, I haven't heard anything like that from my family or anybody else.
